responses.text: {Narration} Tired of waiting for the world to be done with him, Boone ventured into the wastes to make his own way out.
{Narration} Unable to clear his mind of the past, he was at last granted the death he'd awaited, bringing final rest to a life that had ended long ago.
{Narration} As the Battle of Hoover Dam ended, Boone confirmed what he had always suspected - that revenge would never quiet his troubled mind.
{Narration} Side arm in hand, he journeyed back to California in search of the NCR officer who had led the attack on Bitter Springs.
{Narration} There, with only two bullets loaded, Boone did the only thing he believed would put an end to his suffering.
{Narration} Looking for a place where he could be of some use, Boone found himself re-enlisting with his old unit.
{Narration} Though his regrets remained in his thoughts, they coalesced into a purpose, and Boone embraced it.
{Narration} He spent his leave time hunting down slavers in the desert, his First Recon beret the last thing they never saw.
{Narration} Though NCR was withdrawing from the region, Boone remained in New Vegas, finding work as a security guard and caravan scout along the highways.
{Narration} While he might've preferred rejoining his old unit, Boone couldn't bring himself to abandon the city where he'd met his wife.
{Narration} Boone refused to take the Legion's victory lying down.
{Narration} Heading to the hills with his rifle, he began a deadly campaign against high-ranking Legion officers.
{Narration} And though the price on his head rose to levels unheard of, few pursued it, fearing it would be the last thing they'd never see.
{Narration} No longer held in check by his conscience, Boone found lucrative work as a mercenary and assassin.
{Narration} No job was too violent, no target too innocent. As long as the caps were good, Boone would take the job.
{Narration} Driven mad by Caesar's victory at Hoover Dam, and unable to escape his memories, Boone staged a suicide mission against the Legate.
{Narration} Fighting as he wished he would've fought on the day of his wife's death, he brought down scores of Legionaries before being caught.
{Narration} Before his crucifixion, he was brought before the Legate, who expressed his admiration for Boone's reckless abandon.
{Narration} Boone spat tobacco in his eye, for all of Caesar's armies to see.
